core_meaning.short_meaning: Fragrant desert blossom; female companion Rumaytha bint Amr al-Ansariyyah.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Rumaytha (رُمَيْثَة) is a delicate Arabic feminine given name meaning 'a fragrant desert blossom' or 'gentle, sweet-scented plant'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Rumaytha bint Amr al-Ansariyyah, a noble female companion who sat in the presence of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and narrated the famous description of the Seal of Prophethood.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive form of ramth (a sweet-scented desert shrub), conveying affectionate grace, resilience, and pleasant fragrance.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root r-m-th refers to the flowering desert shrub ramth known for its pleasant scent and resilience in Arabian soil. Rumaytha bint Amr was an early Ansari companion from Medina. She was so close to the Prophet's assembly that she reported hearing his words distinctly and seeing the physical Seal of Prophethood (Khatam al-Nubuwwah) between his shoulder blades.
